## Design

### 2026-10-12 – I collected a bunch of reference images (source material, fan art, other 3d prints) of the hex core and analyzed them carefully to figure out the overall geometry. I wanted to figure out how it rotate

**2.72h**

I collected a bunch of reference images (source material, fan art, other 3d prints) of the hex core and analyzed them carefully to figure out the overall geometry. I wanted to figure out how it rotates so smoothly and naturally in the show. Turns out, its essentially just a 3x3 Rubik's cube with custom cubelets (the little cubes the cube is made of).

My plan is to get a Rubik's cube as part of the BOM, get the hex core printed as just the little separate pieces (you can see me labeling them in the timelapse), disassemble the cube, and glue on the printed parts so the final product looks like a hex core, but also turns like a 3x3, _just like the actual hex core does in the show_, so it's even cooler!!

First thing I did was figure out the geometry of the underlying "3x3" in the hex core. I did some really messy calculations to figure out the chamfer amount and piece size based on the size of the cube and the margin I wanted.

![Really messy calculations](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/ebdb2da935d8fe81b9e43e1377fda4fa558842bf11fba42136e429403d8acb33.png)

Then I modeled a simple cube core in CAD based on the dimensions I'd figured out, just to get an idea of what the cube would look like before I glued on the decorations (and to make sure the dimensions were right).

![Core model](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/9c7a7189a528431b0be117df1c380ab0d3fed3d685ee20bd11b5498965ad1162.png)

I identified two types of pieces I needed to model, square pyramid and triangle (they correspond to the differently shaped faces in the model above). The triangle piece would be trivial, so I worked on the square piece, designed a full sketch (took a while, I've never seen so many constraints in one sketch), and finally made the solid. I learnt a lot about Fusion (my CAD software) in the process and regularly had to search up things.

![Square piece sketch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/0d0192991b7534fe18d864ee85ecb46ae4e783a3d3137634d6b3bbf262953581.png)
(All the quadrants except the top right have their details mirrored twice from the top right)

![Square piece solid](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e39272da6c5f95952d0238b3c60ebd77ecd413c1c18da4413a5090e54bd86537.png)

Next, I need to model the triangle pieces and add more details to the square pieces (the glyphs in the original. I'm probably gonna decide/design my own custom symbols/characters to put on there)

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/3ba40b90-873d-49d0-886f-5b2b1d3a194a/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-13 – Today I designed the triangle pieces. This was harder than expected, almost entirely because the design *wasn't entirely rectangles* and designing things is way easier if they're based on rectangles w

**1.23h**

Today I designed the triangle pieces. This was harder than expected, almost entirely because the design *wasn't entirely rectangles* and designing things is way easier if they're based on rectangles with nice 90 degree angles everywhere. Anyways, I modeled the triangle base and outlines with the dimensions I'd calculated last time and added a cube glyph icon thing to the top. I haven't decided yet, but the tentative plan is to print one or two of the triangle pieces with the glyph and the rest without, so the final model doesn't look too cluttered.

![Triangle piece](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/309fa5a8b4115341bb0fd5616013ff14cbcb24f0c0e1b0953a04bd260164b88b.png)

Finally, I also did some planning for the glyphs on the square pieces. The four sides will have letters spelling out "HEXA" on them, in some stylized font, mimicking the look of the original rune glyphs (which I learnt were originally based on LoL's Rune paths).

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/9b763a16-be25-475b-a464-31002826c760/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-17 – Today I made a bunch of progress.

**3.08h**

Today I made a bunch of progress.
- I designed the glyphs for the square pieces. Four stylized letters spelling out "HEXA".

![HEXA](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/9b5f4bb6e8c413ec1411b30ae27f65378d8331c44d2bf0d34a2b02f9b3a1f69f.png)

- I added the letter glyphs to the square piece, scaling and positioned them as perfectly as I could (I spent way too long planning that)

![Square piece](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/930b6e088fab8fc44ab4798c88357ed86f58df5356c81fca611d10fa6799b8b0.png)

- I modified the triangle piece, essentially just scaling it down from having 24mm sides to 20mm sides (This took much longer than I expected, my sketch was really complicated and it kept getting over constrained or messed up in other ways)

- I create a "smooth" triangle piece variant, without the glyph. In the final build, two of the triangle pieces (on opposite corners) will have the glyph and the rest will be blank.

- Finally, I put all the components together into a single design to model what the final outcome would look like with all the pieces attached to the core.

![Full build](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/35d043c168ea5cd513ba46e8c5b0c896563b212691e82c6aa516f9dac5cdd421.png)

In the source material, all the pieces float in place, so it would look something like this, with an invisible core:

![Full build without core](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/9f0c949ddd7b6750f5eac9b86118de6829000830f4b56740b897e16cbcdeb935.png)

The final component count is:
- 1 core
- 18 square pieces
- 2 triangle pieces (with the glyph)
- 6 smooth triangle pieces (without the glyph)

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/cbad742d-fc15-4952-bbc7-a7e9d25d71be/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-18 – Now for the final stretch!

**3.5h**

Now for the final stretch!

First, I modified the glyphs on the square and triangle pieces to be inset 0.5mm instead of extruded 0.5mm. This is, one, so that it looks more like the source material and other recreations, and two, so there's more height variation in the model overall and the glyph designs don't look just like the outlines.

![Square piece](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/400a4e757740bd15b597f8fa51a273434bc7186925e51bd3dc19d84732df92f9.png)

![Triangle piece](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/6e8758eac1cb8d48be915606b572814fe7ee50db4b1cc22c1a58c1e052341d81.png)

Then, I exported all the necessary CAD files for all the models (.step, .f3d, and .stl) and created a folder structure for them to live in. Also, I added images of all the models, and the full build, from different angles.

![Build](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/a8a7c577605d08516898742146474d91548696542f8f8ddbf1da91a1c3732c2d.png)

Then, as I was making the BOM, I did some research into Rubik's cube internals and, long story short, I decided, with great reluctance, to make the final model static. The reasoning is as follows: The cube's pieces are differently shaped than I imagined and so, if I want to keep the final model based on a 3x3, I will have to either:
- Carve away at the cube until its pieces have enough space and are the correct shape for me to glue on the printed parts (this would be very tedious and probably messy, it would be very dependent on the exact shapes and plastic in the pieces, and it could also make the cube very unstable or prone to breaking or popping)
- Design and print the full inner shape, so the entire piece/core can be replaced by my design (this would very time consuming and after printing, might not even function properly)
- Design and print additional "extrusions" that can be attached to the cube which make it bigger and make the overall shape correct for my pieces (this would also be very time consuming and probably not worth the effort because it would add more friction and places for the pieces to lock up)

A very sad day indeed. Since I'm now just making a stationary final model, I also need to print the core shape I designed earlier.

![Core](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e4700ad5d05a90efbf234f2141d2172593629745f3eed269d298538493184009.png)

I'll still print it separately from the other pieces and glue it together later so that the pieces shouldn't need any supports (hopefully). Also, since I'm not building it on top of a 3x3, I decided to scale the whole model up by a factor of about 1.8x so that instead of the whole build being 78mm wide, it's 140mm wide. This is just small enough for the largest piece (the core) to still remain within a 100mmx100mmx100mm footprint (the usual maximum print size).

Finally, after making the (very short) BOM, I also wrote the README for the project.
